fixes.explanation: That's the charge. Dathan and Abiram ask, “Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?” (Numbers 16:13) Watch that little word “also.” They've just said Moses brought them up to kill them in the wilderness, and now they pile this on top. It's like someone who hands you a full list of complaints and then says, "Oh, and another thing."

True, baker. The day after the ground swallowed Korah's men and fire took the 250, the people turn on Moses and Aaron with, “You have killed the LORD’s people!” (Numbers 16:41) After all that, the complaining is right back. I think this one is heavy, and it shows how quickly the grumbling can return.

Two hundred fifty, baker! The text says these men of Israel were “…renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.” (Numbers 16:2) These aren't strangers wandering in off the road. These are the folks with name tags that everybody recognizes. That's 250 big names joining one rebellion against Moses.

No storm in this one, baker. Nothing falls from the sky and no wind blows in Moses' words. He calls it something “unprecedented,” and then he spells it out: the earth opens its mouth, and they go down alive into Sheol. (Numbers 16:30) This is a heavy part of the passage.
